note: Loudspeaker cabinets as circuits (docs/CIRCUIT_ENGINE.md section 10.21): a closed-box air spring on the speaker's cone node plus the acoustic path (cone breakup, cabinet, microphone) as a linear section bank fitted to CC0 cabinet IRs. Referenced as {"type":"sub","of":"lib:<name>","nodes":[<cone node>, <mic node>]}. Generated by tools/circuit/speaker/make_cabs.py; IR credits in each block.

cab-1960ax-g12m25-sm57.note: Marshall 1960AX 4x12 (1998) with Celestion G12M-25 Greenbacks, SM57 on the upper-left speaker. Acoustic path from cone velocity to the microphone, fitted to the open-licence IR jester-emerald/Emerald Pack 1.0/Impulses/48kHz/1_Nacho_Guacamole_48.wav (Jester's Emerald Pack 1.0 by Jester Dyne Productions (Bastian Karschewski), CC0 1.0): the IR divided by the small-signal cone velocity per volt of 4 x G12M25_16 as one 2s2p equivalent driver in this box, smoothed to 1/24 octave, made minimum phase and vector-fitted (Gustavsen-Semlyen) with 24 stable pole pairs (0.67 dB rms, 2.26 dB max error 60 Hz-8 kHz). Attach 'vel' to the cone node of a speaker part with series x parallel = 4 (the box elements load it); 'out' is the mic signal as speaker volts convolved with the IR, times 0.1 (about the speaker voltage in the midband), so a netlist moving from the IR path keeps its level with outputVoltsPerFS x 0.1. Each section is a two-integrator resonator (s = a1, w0) driven from 'vel', so the engine runs it as its own small linear group and the SPICE export is exact.
